narrative.northStar: The Status Side of the Desk
narrative.overview:
The screen reads like the status panel of an automation console. A blue-steel rack-black ground holds slate panels, small legends in a cool grey, and a row of lamps. Every axis and every cue carries a lamp and a word, and the lamp colours are a fixed vocabulary: green ready, amber standby, cyan moving, red clearance. When two pieces come inside clearance, that is the loudest, clearest thing on the screen: the HUD strip itself turns solid red, the clashing axes go red on the bus, the cue row is red-ruled, and a measured white dimension line with its gap in millimetres is drawn in the 3D view. After the cue ends the strip rests on a deep red "Caught" state and a "Caught in Q3" card stays up with a Replay button until it is dismissed.

Colour has two jobs and they never share a hue. Lamps say what state a thing is in. Spike-tape colours, one per axis, say which axis or piece it is, the way a crew marks a deck with coloured tape. The same tape colour follows an axis from its bus cell to its card to the pieces riding it in the 3D view.

The density is a working panel's, not a dashboard's. The right column is a control strip, 380 px on a laptop and wider on big screens. Rows are ruled, not carded. One family, Hanken Grotesk, sets everything in a five-size scale; numbers use tabular figures so a moving readout never jitters. Everything is cut square: controls, bars, cards and the stage overlays have no radius and no drop shadow, and the only circles are the lamps and the Rig guide's step marks. The world's character comes from the palette, the lamp and the tape, not from simulated hardware chrome. STOP is a ramped stop, not an instant E-STOP, so it is a plain saturated red key with nothing around it.

The world rejects the category default: a grey dark dashboard with one accent colour and rounded floating cards.
keyCharacteristics: Rack-black ground with tonal steps for panels, plates and wells; no decorative gradients and no drop shadows.
Flat lamps (a disc with a lighter rim, no glow) always paired with a short word.
One meaning per lamp colour, everywhere in the app; identity is carried by spike tape, never by lamp colours.
One family (Hanken Grotesk) in five sizes; tabular figures for every number.
Square-cut everything; hairline rules separate regions.
The HUD strip changes its whole ground with the state: solid red on a clash, solid amber when stopped, a deep red "Caught" rest after.
Ruled cue sheet with full-width state bands.
The gap is drawn as a drafting dimension in the 3D view, measured from the same data the clearance check uses, and written in millimetres.

rules.name: The One Meaning Rule
rules.body: Each lamp colour means one thing everywhere: green ready/GO, amber standby/held/skipped, cyan moving, red clearance. If a new state does not fit one of those meanings, it gets a neutral treatment and a word, not a borrowed colour.

rules.name: The Steel Selection Rule
rules.body: Selection, focus of attention and the active view are steel, never amber. Amber is spoken for by standby.

rules.name: The Plain Stop Rule
rules.body: STOP is a ramped stop, so it is a plain Stop Red key with a white legend, no collar and no ring. No instant E-STOP control exists in the app; if one is ever added it gets its own treatment, designed then, and STOP does not borrow it.

rules.name: The Spike Tape Rule
rules.body: Identity colour comes from the show's tape palette and answers "which axis or piece?"; lamp colour answers "what state?". Tape appears as a small swatch beside a name or on the piece itself, never as a lamp, a state band, a text colour or a fill behind words. A new axis takes the next free tape colour; never reuse a lamp hue as tape.

rules.name: The Ink On Solid Rule
rules.body: Text on a solid state fill takes that fill's ink (Clash Ink on red, Standby Ink on amber, GO Ink on green), never white or grey, and a lamp on a solid ground of its own colour lights white with an ink ring.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Every number that changes or lines up (cue numbers, times, positions, gaps, counts, units, key caps) is set in Hanken Grotesk with tabular figures (`.tnum`, or `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` on the element). No second face for numbers.

rules.name: The Spent Caps Rule
rules.body: Tracked uppercase is rationed to the Standby legend, tabs, GO / STOP / RESET and the short lamp words (the camera presets FOH / SL / SR / TOP are also upper case, being codes). Everything else is mixed case. A new label is mixed case at 12px, not a new engraved legend.

rules.name: The Five Sizes Rule
rules.body: Type uses 12, 14, 17, 22 and 36 px (`--t-label`, `--t-body`, `--t-title`, `--t-state`, `--t-display`) and nothing between.

rules.name: The Tonal Plate Rule
rules.body: Panels and cards gain depth by stepping up the neutral ramp, never by a shadow. Anything over the 3D stage is solid and ruled.

rules.name: The Flat Lamp Rule
rules.body: A lit lamp is a solid disc in its state colour with a rim mixed 55% toward white. No halo, glow or coloured shadow on a lamp or anything else; state is read from colour plus the word beside it.

rules.name: The Square Cut Rule
rules.body: Everything is cut square. Round means a bulb: the only circles are lamps and the Rig guide's step marks. There is no radius token other than 0 and 50%, and a new component does not get a corner.

rules.name: The Lamp-and-Word Rule
rules.body: A lamp never appears alone. State is never carried by colour only; the word is present at every breakpoint.

rules.name: The Loudest Strip Rule
rules.body: A live conflict is the loudest thing on the screen, and the HUD strip carries it: solid red, not a small lamp on a quiet strip. Nothing else is allowed a solid red ground.

rules.name: The Ruled Sheet Rule
rules.body: The cue list is a sheet, not a stack of cards: 1px Hairline Rule between rows, state carried by full-width bands.

rules.name: The Live Versus Minimum Rule
rules.body: A gap number is always labelled with what it is: "now" for the live gap while pieces are moving, "min" for the closest approach the check recorded (badges, Caught card, log). Two unlabelled gap numbers never share the screen.

rules.name: The Millimetre Rule
rules.body: Gaps and clearance are shown in millimetres, the unit of a drawing, a Vectorworks model and a tape measure: whole mm from 10 up, one decimal below (6.4 mm), "CONTACT" at zero. Metres stay in the data and the show JSON; `formatGap` and `formatClearance` in `src/ui/format.js` are the only places the unit changes.

rules.name: The Measured Line Rule
rules.body: Any drawn gap, pose or conflict comes from the same data the clearance check uses. Never draw an approximate or decorative indicator; the 24px floor stretches only the drawing, never the number.

dos: **Do** pair every lamp with a short word, at every breakpoint.
**Do** keep each lamp colour to its one meaning: green ready/GO, amber standby/held/skipped, cyan moving, red clearance.
**Do** carry axis and piece identity in spike-tape colours from the show data, as a small swatch beside a name or on the piece.
**Do** let a live conflict take the whole HUD strip: solid Clash Red, Clash Ink text.
**Do** keep the Caught resting state and card up after the cue, until dismissed, the next GO or RESET.
**Do** write gaps in millimetres and label them "now" or "min".
**Do** mark selection and the active view with Steel and a 2px Steel underline.
**Do** set every number in Hanken Grotesk with tabular figures.
**Do** separate regions with 1px Hairline Rule and step depth with the neutral ramp.
**Do** cut every control, bar and card square; keep circles for lamps and guide marks.
**Do** use the white 2px focus ring with its black halo on everything focusable, inset where an edge would clip it.
**Do** keep touch targets at 44px on coarse pointers, and on the phone dock one bar under the bus.
**Do** stay within the five type sizes (12, 14, 17, 22, 36 px).
donts: **Don't** use amber for selection, hover or general warnings; it means standby.
**Don't** wrap STOP in a collar or ring, or give it an instant E-STOP look; it is a ramped stop.
**Don't** use Clash Red for anything that is not a clearance conflict.
**Don't** use a lamp colour as spike tape, or tape as a state colour, band or text colour.
**Don't** add a second typeface, or set new tracked-uppercase legends beyond the Standby legend, tabs, transport and lamp words.
**Don't** turn the cue list into cards, or put the main panel content in floating rounded cards.
**Don't** add drop shadows, glow, halos or coloured shadows to lamps or anything else; overlays are opaque and ruled.
**Don't** round a corner, except a lamp and the Rig guide's step marks.
**Don't** draw a gap or conflict indicator that is not computed by the clearance check, or show a gap without saying whether it is live or minimum.
**Don't** abbreviate the clash word to CLR, or call an axis at its target IDLE.
